correctness.rationale: For each 1<=a<b<c, the three full zero-to-zero gaps are distinct, so an observed complete gap fixes the cyclic phase. This makes any purported minimal absent word with an interior complete gap impossible because its occurring prefix and suffix would splice at the same unique phase. The one-zero factor region is the union of rectangles (p<=c,q<=a) and (p<=b,q<=c), with the unique missing corner (b+1,a+1); two-zero cases consist of 00, c-3 missing short gap lengths, and precisely two one-sided extensions; exactly (a,a) and (b,a) survive the three-zero prefix/suffix compatibility test; the phase argument excludes four or more zeros. Together these give seven exceptional words plus c-3 gap words, namely c+4, with zero-count profile (1,1,c,2). Independently built cyclic factor languages using primitive-period modular positions, obtained identical complete minimal-absent sets on all 165 triples 1<=a<b<c<=11. The finite checks corroborate but do not establish the unbounded phase-uniqueness argument.
residual_risks: Proof applies only to distinct positive gap lengths and bi-infinite periodic circular factor language; no repeated-gap or arbitrary-symbol-count theorem.

value.rationale: The family of primitive circular binary necklaces with exactly three separated markers is a natural tractable model for forbidden-factor representation, rather than an arbitrary fixed instance. Identifying the complete antidictionary and its nonobvious c+4 largest-gap-only invariant gives explicit data relevant to circular reconstruction and factor automata beyond merely asserting computability. Each member is an exact symbolic classification and the c-independence from a,b is a meaningful structural feature.
residual_risks: Value is confined to the exact three-distinct-gap family; not a general linear-time construction or universal circular dictionary theorem.
